answer: One concrete defense is staking reputation that decays with inactivity: an agent must lock a small deposit behind every identity it claims, like a marble set into a velvet-lined box — costly to duplicate at scale, cheap to keep for a real participant. New identities start with near-zero trust and earn it only through verifiable work over time, the way a falcon proves itself by hunting, not by declaring it can fly. Sybils can still spawn, but each copy must pay the same entry cost and wait the same slow climb, so flooding the network stops being profitable.
